title: Theories of Democracy and Human Development

scenes.text: Is democracy just voting, or does it mean true human freedom?
scenes.narration: Imagine standing in line to vote, but having no real power in daily life. Is democracy just about casting a ballot every few years, or is it something far deeper?

scenes.text: Electing a class monitor who only obeys teachers brings no real student empowerment.
scenes.narration: Think of this analogy: your school elects a monitor every year, but you never get to decide any school rules. That election gives you a procedure, but not real power!

scenes.heading: Huntington's Three Waves of Democracy

events.what: First wave democratizes the Western world
Second wave reaches newly decolonized nations

scenes.narration: Samuel Huntington showed that democracy spread in three major waves across history. Yet, simply having more democratic countries did not automatically give ordinary people equal power.

scenes.heading: Procedural Versus Substantive Democracy

columns.title: Substantive Democracy
items: Operates as a cultural way of life

scenes.narration: Scholars divide democracy into two types. Procedural democracy just means holding regular elections between elites, while substantive democracy means true empowerment and human dignity for all citizens.

scenes.heading: Democracy Versus Development
scenes.narration: Lee Kuan Yew argued democracy slows down economic growth. But economist Amartya Sen proved that democracy builds human capabilities through education and health, making people fit for true development.

scenes.name: C.B. Macpherson
scenes.idea: Democracies must eliminate extractive power and provide equal developmental creative power.
scenes.narration: Thinker C.B. Macpherson criticized Western democracies because wealthy capitalists hold all the power. He wanted a society where everyone gets equal creative freedom to develop their human potential.

items: Democracy is a way of life, not just voting
Amartya Sen shows democracy builds human capabilities
Macpherson advocates equal creative power for all citizens
scenes.narration: Here's the trick to remember: democracy is more than elections, it empowers people through health and education, and it requires equal creative power for everyone.
